newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle markets quiet, $70 passed - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle markets quiet, $70 passed - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet Wednesday, with feedlot managers from Kansas to Texas still passing $70.00 per cwt bids, feedlot sources said.

Cattle feeders continue to price cattle at $73.00, but would trade at $72.00, some sources said. A small number of Kansas steers and heifers sold Tuesday at $73.00, but feedlots said they probably were for up-scale branded beef programs.
Most cattle sold last week have been shipped but a few feedlots said some shipments were scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday.
A few heifers in Kansas traded at $70.00 early Wednesday but sources said the cattle were not well finished.
USDA reported beef cutout values closed Tuesday up $2.00 to $2.14 per cwt on choice cuts and up $0.69 to $0.78 for select cuts.
Cutout values for choice 1-3 700-850 lb carcasses were quoted at $118.89 per cwt, which USDA said was the highest level since June 1993.
